accepted.s: The United Nations Human Rights Council was established in 2006 by replacing which body?
o: United Nations Commission on Human Rights
United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
accepted.x: The UN Human Rights Council was formed in 2006 as the successor to the UN Commission on Human Rights.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional succession clue to distinguish the Council from other UN bodies.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: The headquarters of the United Nations Human Rights Council is located at:
accepted.x: The UN Human Rights Council is based in Geneva.
accepted.tq: Test the location of the specific UN human rights institution rather than its associated conference.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the UN Human Rights Council:
1. It consists of 47 members.
2. Its members are elected by the UN General Assembly.
3. Members are elected for three-year terms.
4. A member may serve an unlimited number of consecutive terms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Council has 47 members elected by the UN General Assembly for three-year terms. A member can serve at most two consecutive terms, making statement 4 false.
accepted.tq: Find the false duration statement by checking the limit on consecutive terms.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: A member of the UN Human Rights Council may be suspended for gross violations of human rights by:
o: A unanimous decision of the Human Rights Council
A two-thirds vote of the UN General Assembly
A decision of the International Court of Justice
A simple majority vote of the Security Council
accepted.x: The UN General Assembly may suspend a Council member for gross and systematic violations through a two-thirds vote.
accepted.tq: Ask which authority exercises the power and what voting threshold applies.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the regional distribution of seats in the UN Human Rights Council.

List-I (Region)
a. Africa
b. Asia-Pacific
c. Latin America and the Caribbean

List-II (Seats)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the number of seats allotted to Western Europe and Others in the UN Human Rights Council?
accepted.x: Western Europe and Others has seven seats in the UN Human Rights Council.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the closely placed regional seat figures.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: India was a member of the UN Human Rights Council during which of the following periods?
accepted.x: India served on the Council during 2019–21 and again during 2022–24.
accepted.tq: Use the paired-term chronology to distinguish the two specified Indian memberships.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly describes the Universal Periodic Review (UPR)?
o: It examines only the implementation of economic and social rights.
It is a peer review of the human rights record of every UN member state.
It is a judicial review conducted only for states accused of treaty violations.
It is a review conducted by the International Court of Justice every three years.
accepted.x: The UPR is a peer review of the human rights record of every UN member state, conducted under the Human Rights Council.
accepted.tq: Distinguish universal peer review from judicial or treaty-specific review.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: The Universal Periodic Review has been conducted since 2008 in cycles of approximately:
accepted.x: The UPR has operated since 2008 in cycles of about four and a half years.
accepted.tq: Test the approximate cycle length against the nearby standard periodic intervals.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights was set up in 1993 following the:
accepted.x: The OHCHR was established in 1993 after the Vienna Conference.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with the conference that preceded its establishment.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: In 2026, the Global Alliance for Human Rights convened by the OHCHR used which model?
accepted.x: The Global Alliance for Human Rights used the Imagine–Dialogue–Act model in preparation for the UDHR's 80th anniversary in December 2028.
accepted.tq: Test the exact three-part formulation associated with the current initiative.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes treaty bodies from special rapporteurs in the UN human rights machinery?
o: Treaty bodies are organs of the General Assembly, whereas special rapporteurs are organs of the Security Council.
Treaty bodies are courts, whereas special rapporteurs are elected representatives of states.
Treaty bodies are committees of independent experts monitoring core treaties, whereas special rapporteurs are unpaid independent experts on a country or theme.
Treaty bodies review only refugee matters, whereas special rapporteurs review only economic rights.
accepted.x: Treaty bodies are committees of independent experts that monitor core treaties. Special rapporteurs are unpaid independent experts appointed under the Human Rights Council's special procedures to examine a theme or country.
accepted.tq: Separate the two similar mechanisms by their composition and mandate.
accepted.sec: UN human rights machinery - Human Rights Council, UPR, OHCHR, treaty bodies, special rapporteurs

accepted.s:
Match the following rights with the year or date of their recognition by the UN General Assembly.

a. Right to development
a. 1986
b. Right to water and sanitation
c. Right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment

1. 28 July 2010
2. 28 July 2022
3. 1986

Select the correct combination:
accepted.x: The Right to Development was recognised in 1986; the Right to Water and Sanitation on 28 July 2010; and the Right to a Clean, Healthy and Sustainable Environment on 28 July 2022.
accepted.tq: Anchor the two exact July dates first and then match the remaining year.
accepted.sec: Rights newly recognised by the UN General Assembly → year

accepted.s: On 28 July 2022, the United Nations General Assembly recognised which of the following as a universal human right?
o: Right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment
accepted.x: The UN General Assembly recognised the right to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment as a universal human right on 28 July 2022.
accepted.tq: Use the precise official formulation rather than a broader environmental phrase.
accepted.sec: Rights newly recognised by the UN General Assembly → year

accepted.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly in:
accepted.x: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly in 1948.
accepted.tq: Separate the adoption year of the UDHR from the later adoption year of the Covenants.
accepted.sec: UDHR - date, drafting chair, articles, rights included and not included, Human Rights Day

accepted.s: Who chaired the drafting committee of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
accepted.x: Eleanor Roosevelt chaired the drafting committee of the UDHR.
accepted.tq: Identify the person associated specifically with chairing the drafting committee.
accepted.sec: UDHR - date, drafting chair, articles, rights included and not included, Human Rights Day

accepted.s: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights contains:
o: 25 articles covering only social and economic rights
20 articles covering only civil and political rights
30 articles covering civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights
accepted.x: The UDHR contains 30 articles covering civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights.
accepted.tq: Combine the article count with the full range of rights covered.
accepted.sec: UDHR - date, drafting chair, articles, rights included and not included, Human Rights Day

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT specifically included among the rights recognised in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
o: Right to an adequate standard of living
accepted.x: The listed UDHR rights include dignity, liberty, equality, life, an adequate standard of living and education. A right to universal basic income is not included.
accepted.tq: Find the entitlement that falls outside the stated UDHR list.
accepted.sec: UDHR - date, drafting chair, articles, rights included and not included, Human Rights Day

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Universal Declaration of Human Rights:
1. It is a treaty.
2. It is legally binding in the same manner as a ratified international covenant.
3. It covers civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights.
Which of the statements given above is correct?
accepted.x: Statement 3 is correct because the UDHR covers all five categories of rights listed. Statements 1 and 2 are false: the UDHR is not a treaty and is not legally binding as a treaty.
accepted.tq: Reject the treaty and legal-bindingness traps while retaining the accurate scope statement.
accepted.sec: UDHR - date, drafting chair, articles, rights included and not included, Human Rights Day

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding privacy and international human rights law is correct?
o: Privacy is protected by Article 12 of the UDHR and Article 17 of the ICCPR.
Privacy was included only in the ICESCR and not in the UDHR.
Privacy is protected only by Article 19 of the ICCPR.
Privacy is protected by neither the UDHR nor the ICCPR.
accepted.x: The UDHR protects privacy under Article 12 and the ICCPR protects it under Article 17.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the correct privacy provisions from the commonly confused expression-rights provision.
accepted.sec: UDHR - date, drafting chair, articles, rights included and not included, Human Rights Day

accepted.s: Human rights are best understood as rights which are:
o: Limited to civil and political entitlements
Inherent and inalienable, held simply because a person is human
Available only to citizens of democratic states
accepted.x: Human rights are inherent and inalienable rights possessed simply by virtue of being human.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining features rather than a source-based or citizenship-based limitation.
accepted.sec: Concept of human rights - dignity, universalism, indivisibility, which entitlements count

accepted.s: Which principle of human rights signifies that they apply across cultures and to all persons?
accepted.x: Universalism means that human rights belong to all persons across cultures. Human rights are also grounded in human dignity.
accepted.tq: Match the principle with its defining meaning.
accepted.sec: Concept of human rights - dignity, universalism, indivisibility, which entitlements count

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Civil-political rights and socio-economic rights are indivisible and interdependent.
2. The Vienna Declaration of 1993 affirmed the indivisibility and interdependence of human rights.
3. Human rights are confined to rights expressly declared Fundamental Rights in the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because human rights are broader than constitutional Fundamental Rights.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional-scope statement as the false comparison against the Vienna principle.
accepted.sec: Concept of human rights - dignity, universalism, indivisibility, which entitlements count

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between human rights and Fundamental Rights in India?
o: The two expressions are legally identical in every respect.
Every Fundamental Right is a human right, but not every human right is a Fundamental Right.
Every human right is a Fundamental Right, but no Fundamental Right is a human right.
Neither Fundamental Rights nor statutory rights can be human rights.
accepted.x: Every Fundamental Right is a human right, but the wider category of human rights is not limited to constitutionally guaranteed Fundamental Rights.
accepted.tq: Test the inclusion relationship rather than treating the two categories as identical.
accepted.sec: Concept of human rights - dignity, universalism, indivisibility, which entitlements count

accepted.s: The right to vote in India is classified as:
o: A Fundamental Right under Part III
A statutory right under Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act
A Directive Principle of State Policy
A natural right beyond statutory regulation
accepted.x: The right to vote is a statutory right under Section 62 of the Representation of the People Act, not a Fundamental Right.
accepted.tq: Distinguish statutory rights from Fundamental Rights by identifying the governing provision.
accepted.sec: Concept of human rights - dignity, universalism, indivisibility, which entitlements count

accepted.s: The classification of human rights into three generations was proposed by:
accepted.x: Karel Vasak proposed the three-generation classification of human rights in 1977.
accepted.tq: Match the classification with its proponent and avoid confusing the proponent with the UDHR drafter.
accepted.sec: Generations of human rights → proponent and rights

accepted.s: Karel Vasak's three generations of human rights are associated respectively with:
accepted.x: The first, second and third generations were mapped respectively to liberty, equality and fraternity or solidarity.
accepted.tq: Recall the organising values of the three-generation classification.
accepted.sec: Generations of human rights → proponent and rights

accepted.s:
Match the generation of human rights with its principal category.

List-I
 a. First generation
 b. Second generation
 c. Third generation

List-II
 i. Collective rights such as peace and development
 ii. Civil and political rights
 iii. Economic, social and cultural rights

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: First-generation rights are civil and political; second-generation rights are economic, social and cultural; third-generation rights are collective rights such as peace and development.

accepted.sec: Generations of human rights → proponent and rights

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a third-generation human right?
accepted.x: The right to a healthy environment is a collective or solidarity-based third-generation right.
accepted.tq: Separate collective rights from first-generation civil and political rights.
accepted.sec: Generations of human rights → proponent and rights

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The generations of human rights are mutually exclusive.
2. Education may be classified as both a second-generation and a third-generation right.
3. The first generation primarily comprises civil and political rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is false because the generations overlap rather than being mutually exclusive.
accepted.tq: Spot the absolute claim that conflicts with the overlap among generations.
accepted.sec: Generations of human rights → proponent and rights

accepted.s: The International Bill of Human Rights comprises:
o: The ICCPR, ICESCR and the Vienna Declaration only
Only the UDHR and the ICCPR
The UDHR, UN Charter and International Court of Justice Statute
The UDHR, ICCPR, ICESCR and the optional protocols
accepted.x: The International Bill of Human Rights consists of the UDHR, the ICCPR, the ICESCR and the optional protocols.
accepted.tq: Test the complete composition of a named international instrument group.
accepted.sec: International Bill of Human Rights - components, ICCPR and ICESCR, optional protocols

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: ICCPR — adopted on 23 March 1976 and entered into force on 16 December 1966
ICESCR — adopted on 16 December 1966 and entered into force on 3 January 1976
ICESCR — adopted on 3 January 1976 and entered into force on 16 December 1966
ICCPR — adopted on 16 December 1966 and entered into force on 3 January 1976
accepted.x: The ICESCR was adopted on 16 December 1966 and entered into force on 3 January 1976. The ICCPR entered into force on 23 March 1976.
accepted.tq: Separate the common adoption date from the different entry-into-force dates.
accepted.sec: International Bill of Human Rights - components, ICCPR and ICESCR, optional protocols

accepted.s: Which of the following rights is associated with the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights?
o: Work, social security, health and education, realised progressively
accepted.x: The ICESCR covers work, social security, health and education, with these rights realised progressively. The other options refer to ICCPR provisions.
accepted.tq: Separate the economic-social covenant from the civil-political covenant by its subject matter.
accepted.sec: International Bill of Human Rights - components, ICCPR and ICESCR, optional protocols

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the ICCPR?
accepted.x: Article 19 of the ICCPR concerns expression. Privacy is protected under Article 17; the other three pairings are correct.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped article number in the list of ICCPR rights.
accepted.sec: International Bill of Human Rights - components, ICCPR and ICESCR, optional protocols

accepted.s:
Match the optional protocol with its principal subject.

List-I
 a. First Optional Protocol to the ICCPR
 b. Second Optional Protocol to the ICCPR
 c. Optional Protocol to the ICESCR

List-II
 i. Complaints procedure
 ii. Abolition of the death penalty
 iii. Complaints procedure

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The First Optional Protocol to the ICCPR provides for individual complaints, the Second Optional Protocol concerns abolition of the death penalty, and the ICESCR Optional Protocol provides a complaints mechanism.
accepted.tq: Lock the death-penalty pair first, then distinguish the two complaints protocols by their parent covenant.
accepted.sec: International Bill of Human Rights - components, ICCPR and ICESCR, optional protocols

accepted.s: The First and Second Optional Protocols to the ICCPR were adopted in:
accepted.x: The First Optional Protocol to the ICCPR was adopted in 1966, while the Second Optional Protocol was adopted in 1989.
accepted.tq: Arrange the protocol years by distinguishing the two ICCPR protocols from the ICESCR protocol.
accepted.sec: International Bill of Human Rights - components, ICCPR and ICESCR, optional protocols

accepted.s: India's position concerning the ICCPR First Optional Protocol is correctly stated as follows:
o: India signed the First Optional Protocol in 1979 and permits direct UN complaints without domestic remedies.
India has not been a party to the ICCPR since its adoption.
India has been a party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed the First Optional Protocol.
India is party only to the Second Optional Protocol and not to the ICCPR.
accepted.x: India has been a party to the ICCPR since 1979 but has not signed its First Optional Protocol. Consequently, individuals in India cannot use that protocol's UN complaints procedure after exhausting domestic remedies.
accepted.tq: Separate membership in the parent covenant from signature of its optional protocol.
accepted.sec: International Bill of Human Rights - components, ICCPR and ICESCR, optional protocols
